(b)	During the year, no report under sub-section (12) of section 143 of the Companies Act, 2013 has been filed by cost auditor/ secretarial auditor or by us in Form ADT – 4 as prescribed under Rule 13 of Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 with the Central Government.

statutory_dues.text:
Annexure 1 (vii)(a)	Undisputed statutory dues including goods and services tax, provident fund, employees’ state insurance, income-tax, sales-tax, service tax, duty of excise, value added tax, duty of custom, cess and other material statutory dues applicable to the Company have generally been regularly deposited with the appropriate authorities though there has been a slight delay in a few cases. 
		According to the information and explanations given to us and based on audit procedures performed by us, no undisputed amounts payable in respect of these statutory dues were outstanding, at the year end, for a period of more than six months from the date they became payable.

call_points.text: Monocon targeted to return to breakeven by Q4FY27 after losing a key UK customer.
Hofmann expected to move closer to breakeven as FY27 progresses.
Gujarat greenfield still awaits Press Note 3 approval from the Government of India.
call_points.versus_prior: no approval yet; earlier call flagged the same regulatory wait

call_points.text: Khurda greenfield work has picked up; board still evaluating pace and structure of investment.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterated: Khurda dolomite bricks project from the Q4FY26 call

call_points.text: US revenue grew 26% in Q4FY26 and 25% in FY26, with margins at high-teen levels.
Domestic revenue reached ₹864 Cr, up 20% for FY26 and 7% in Q4.
Consolidated EBITDA margin was 8.6% in Q4FY26 and 7.7% for FY26.
Exports fell 11% in FY26 on geopolitical uncertainty and weak external demand.
Consolidated debt ₹195.6 Cr against cash of ₹122 Cr as of March 31, 2026.
Board recommended a dividend of ₹2.15 per share, 21.5% of face value.
Legacy goodwill fully amortised; FY27 earnings lose a ~₹26.7 Cr annual non-cash charge.
Analyst pressed on top-level exits; MD called it normal churn after the old CEO left.
Raw material costs hinge on imported minerals and volatile shipping rates, with no hedge disclosed.
**Global outlook:** Global steel demand is expected to bottom out during 2025-2026 and return to growth, with India remaining the fastest-growing major steel market.
**New projects:** Greenfield projects initiated at Khurdha (Dolomite Bricks, ₹300-350 Cr) and Gujarat (Basic Bricks, ₹300 Cr) targeting FY28/FY29.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has filed a Writ Petition (WPO No. 506 of 2024) before the Hon’ble High Court at Calcutta, challenging the Order under Section 148A and the Notice issued under Section 148 for AY 2018-19. The dispute pertains to the deduction of Rs. 5,006 lakhs claimed by the Company on account of depreciation on goodwill arising from amalgamation, with the tax involved amounting to Rs. 1,732 lakhs. The Hon’ble Court has heard the petition and passed an order directing that no further steps be taken by the respondents based on the notice issued under Section 148 until the disposal of the Writ Petition.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Ward 5(1), Kolkata

timeline.summary: On 2nd May 2026, IFGL Refractories announced that shareholders approved the appointment of Mihir Prakash Bajoria as Managing Director for three years.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹482.97 Cr (+7.7% YoY), net profit ₹14.28 Cr (+69.4% YoY).
On June 1, 2026, IFGL Refractories published its Q4 & FY26 investor presentation highlighting consolidated revenue of ₹1,904 Cr and strategic capex plans.
IFGL Refractories Limited’s 4QFY26 Earnings Conference Call held on June 2, 2026, at 5:00 PM IST via Monarch Networth Capital.

IFGL Refractories terminated its October 14, 2024 JV agreement with Marvels International Group (Seychelles) on October 14, 2026; Marvel never subscribed to its 49%, so IFGL-Marvels Refractories Limited remains wholly owned by IFGL.
